'''''Ageratina havanensis''''', the '''Havana snakeroot'''<ref>{{PLANTS |symbol=AGHA4 |taxon=Ageratina havanensis}}</ref> or '''white mistflower''',<ref>[https://npsot.org/wp/wilco/2013/02/05/ageratina-havanensis-white-mistflower/ Williamson County Chapter (NPSOT-Wilco) Native Plant Society of Texas, ''Ageratina havanensis'' – White Mistflower]</ref> is a species of [[Flowering plant|flowering]] [[shrub]] in the family [[Asteraceae]], native to the south-western United States ([[Texas]]), Cuba, and north-eastern and east-central Mexico ([[Veracruz]], [[Tamaulipas]], [[Coahuila]], [[Nuevo León]], [[Hidalgo (state)|Hidalgo]], [[San Luis Potosí]], [[Puebla]], [[Guanajuato]], [[Querétaro]]).<ref>{{cite book | author=George Diggs |author2=Barney Lipscomb |author3=Robert O'Kennon |title=Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas|isbn=978-1-889878-01-0|year=1999|publisher=Botanical Research Institute of Texas |url= http://artemis.austincollege.edu/acad/bio/gdiggs/NCTXpdf.htm }}</ref> Unlike many other species of ''Ageratina'', it is evergreen.<ref>{{eFloras|1|250066014|Ageratina havanensis |first=Guy L. |last=Nesom |volume=21}}</ref><ref>{{BONAP |genus=Ageratina |species=havanensis |date=2014}}</ref><ref>Turner, B. L. 1997. The Comps of Mexico: A systematic account of the family Asteraceae, vol. 1 -- Eupatorieae. Phytologia Memoirs 11: i–iv, 1–272</ref><ref>Turner, B. L. 2010. Phytologia 92:388-399</ref>

==Etymology==
''Ageratina'' is derived from [[Greek language|Greek]] meaning 'un-aging', in reference to the flowers keeping their color for a long time. This name was used by [[Dioscorides]] for a number of different plants.<ref name="gledhill">Gledhill, David (2008). "The Names of Plants". Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|9780521866453}} (hardback), {{ISBN|9780521685535}} (paperback).  pp 39</ref>
